questions.stem: Match each transformation to its name. P: a = 3 * 4 becomes a = 12. Q: y = x * 8 becomes y = x << 3. R: after b = c, a later d = b + 1 becomes d = c + 1. S: x = x * 1 is deleted. Names: 1 constant folding, 2 strength reduction, 3 copy propagation, 4 algebraic simplification.
questions.explanation: Evaluating 3 * 4 at compile time is constant folding. Replacing a multiply by a shift is strength reduction. Replacing a use of b by the c it was copied from is copy propagation. Removing x = x * 1 uses the identity x × 1 = x, which is algebraic simplification.

questions.stem: Flow graph: B1: a = read(); b = read() → B2. B2: c = a + b; if c > 10 goto B4 else B3. B3: a = c − 1; d = b * 2 → B5. B4: d = a + 1 → B5. B5: e = d + c; if e < 100 goto B2, else exit. No variable is live at exit. Which variables are live at the entry of B4?
questions.explanation: Iterating IN = USE ∪ (OUT − DEF) backward to a fixpoint gives IN[B2] = {a, b}, IN[B5] = {a, b, c, d}, IN[B3] = {b, c}. B4 uses a and defines d, and OUT[B4] = IN[B5] = {a, b, c, d}, so IN[B4] = {a} ∪ {a, b, c} = {a, b, c}. c is live because B5 reads it, b because the back edge to B2 reads it. d is defined in B4 before any use, so it is dead at entry.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly describes reaching-definitions analysis?
options: Forward analysis; union at merge points
Backward analysis; union at merge points
Forward analysis; intersection at merge points
Backward analysis; intersection at merge points
questions.explanation: A definition reaches a point if it survives along some path from the definition to that point, so facts flow forward with the program and combine by union (a may analysis). Backward with union describes liveness; forward with intersection describes available expressions.

questions.stem: The straight-line code x = a + b; y = x * c; x = y − a; y = x + y; z = x * y is converted to static single assignment form. Counting the input variables a, b and c, how many distinct variable names does the SSA code use?
questions.explanation: Each assignment gets a fresh version: x1 = a + b; y1 = x1 * c; x2 = y1 − a; y2 = x2 + y1; z1 = x2 * y2. That is 5 new names (x1, y1, x2, y2, z1) plus the 3 read-only inputs a, b, c, for 8 names in all. No φ-functions are needed because there is no join point.

questions.stem: B1: if p goto B2 else B3. B2: x = 3; y = 5; goto B4. B3: x = 3; y = 7. B4: z = x + y; w = x * 2. The value of p is unknown at compile time. After data-flow constant propagation, which statement about B4 is correct?
options: x and w are constants (3 and 6); y and z are not constants
x, y, z and w are all constants
Only x is a constant; w is not, because it is computed after the join
None of x, y, z, w is a constant, because B4 has two predecessors
questions.explanation: At the join, x meets 3 ∧ 3 = 3, while y meets 5 ∧ 7 = NAC. Then z = x + y has a NAC operand and is NAC, while w = x * 2 folds to 6. Constant propagation requires agreement on every path, which is why a join with different constants yields NAC.

questions.stem: Loop-invariant code motion finds t = a * b inside a loop, where neither a nor b is assigned in the loop. Where is the computation placed so that it executes once?
options: In a preheader block that runs once before control enters the header
In the block holding the back edge to the header
questions.explanation: The header is part of the loop and runs on every iteration, so code there still repeats. A preheader is inserted on the edges entering the header from outside the loop, so it runs exactly once per entry into the loop. The latch also runs every iteration, and the exit block runs after the loop, too late for uses inside it.

questions.stem: B1: if p goto B2 else B3. B2: x = a + b; y = c * d; goto B4. B3: z = a + b; c = c + 1. B4: u = a + b; v = c * d. Which computations in B4 can global common subexpression elimination replace by a previously computed value?
options: Both u = a + b and v = c * d
Neither, because B4 has two predecessors
questions.explanation: Available expressions meet by intersection. OUT[B2] = {a + b, c * d}. B3 computes a + b and then assigns c, which kills c * d (and c + 1), so OUT[B3] = {a + b}. IN[B4] = OUT[B2] ∩ OUT[B3] = {a + b}. So u can reuse a temporary set by a + b on both paths, while c * d is not available along B3 and v must be recomputed.

pitfalls.text: Every S-attributed SDD is L-attributed, but an L-attributed SDD with an inherited attribute is not S-attributed; an inherited attribute that reads a right sibling makes the SDD neither.
A labelled jump target starts a new basic block; the previous block ends at the instruction just before it, not at the label.
Liveness runs backward with union; reaching definitions runs forward with union; available expressions runs forward with intersection. Mixing the directions gives wrong sets.
Triples have no result field: a result is named by its position, so reordering triples breaks references, which is what indirect triples avoid.
In SDT trace questions the grammar fixes precedence; an operator that looks like + may bind looser than one that looks like ×.
With call by reference or value-result and the same variable passed twice, the formals alias; trace the shared cell, and for value-result the copy-out order.
Loop-invariant code goes to the preheader, not the header: the header runs every iteration.

errata.claim: Translating x = a + b * c − d needs 3 temporaries, explained as one per binary operator (2) plus the final assignment.
errata.correction: The statement has three binary operators (*, + and −), not two, and the final copy into x needs no temporary of its own. With a fresh temporary per operator the code is t1 = b * c; t2 = a + t1; t3 = t2 − d; x = t3, so 3 temporaries. Writing the last result straight into x needs 2, and reusing temporaries needs only 1.

errata.claim: Constant propagation is a forward may-analysis.
errata.correction: It is forward, but a variable counts as constant at a point only if every path reaching that point gives it the same constant (c₁ ∧ c₂ = NAC for c₁ ≠ c₂). That all-paths requirement makes it a must-style analysis, and the framework is monotone but not distributive.

errata.claim: Loop-invariant code motion moves invariant computations to the loop header.
errata.correction: The header belongs to the loop and executes on every iteration. Invariant code is moved to a preheader, a new block placed on the edges entering the header from outside the loop, so it runs once per entry into the loop.

errata.claim: A basic block ends at a branch or at a label.
errata.correction: A block ends at a branch or just before a labelled instruction. The labelled instruction is a jump target, hence a leader, and starts the next block.
